title: East Brunswick Declares October Hindu Heritage Month, Sets Two Diwali Celebrations
excerpt: Mayor Brad Cohen and the Township Council presented the proclamation on October 12; a Mega Diwali festival on October 24 and a municipal lighting ceremony on October 30 are open to all residents.
body:
• East Brunswick, New Jersey has officially recognized October 2026 as Hindu Heritage Month, with a proclamation presented by Mayor Brad Cohen and the Township Council on October 12.
  • Two public celebrations follow: UDNJ's Mega Diwali 2026 on Saturday, October 24, noon to 8:30 p.m., and the township's Diwali lighting ceremony on Friday, October 30 at 6:30 p.m. at the Municipal Complex, 1 Civic Center Drive.
  • The proclamation follows New Jersey's 2024 designation of October as Hindu Heritage Month statewide.
  • Diwali and the Hindu New Year fall in early November this year, after October's Navratri, Durga Puja and Dussehra observances.

East Brunswick has formally recognized October 2026 as Hindu Heritage Month, honouring the traditions, values and contributions of its Hindu American residents. Mayor Brad Cohen and the Township Council presented the proclamation on Monday, October 12, joined by members of the Hindu community, according to TAPinto East Brunswick. Councilman Dinesh Behal presented the proclamation.

What the Proclamation Recognizes

The document recognizes Sanatana Dharma — Hinduism — as one of the world's oldest living religious and philosophical traditions, and cites Hindu contributions to science, mathematics, medicine, the arts, education, business and public service. It names the principles of seva (service), ahimsa (nonviolence) and shanti (peace), and the influence of yoga, Ayurveda, the Bhagavad Gita and the Upanishads. Behal described Hindu residents as neighbours, business owners, educators and leaders, and invoked Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam — the world is one family — as the value behind the recognition.

The township's move follows the state's lead: New Jersey designated October as Hindu Heritage Month in 2024. East Brunswick's own school district is among the New Jersey districts that close for Diwali, a measure of how established the community is in this part of Middlesex County.

"A proclamation can seem a simple gesture but for our community it means a great deal."

— Divik Bhasin, United Desi of New Jersey

Community Response

Shweta Patil, speaking for United Desi of New Jersey (UDNJ) and the East Brunswick Hindu community, thanked the mayor and council and stressed the importance of preserving and sharing traditions with younger generations and the wider community. Divik Bhasin, also of UDNJ, said the recognition affirms that the community's festivals, music, food, faith and values are part of the township's identity — particularly for younger residents growing up between two cultures.

Mayor Cohen described East Brunswick as extraordinarily diverse and pointed to how the township has adapted to its residents: support for cricket facilities used by the growing South Asian community, backing for local cultural celebrations, and a recent appearance in nearby New Brunswick by Sri Sri Ravi Shankar of the Art of Living Foundation. His message was that residents can keep their cultural roots while embracing an American identity. Council President Dana Zimbicki thanked Hindu residents for their service and volunteering, citing seva specifically.

Two Diwali Events Open to Everyone

The recognition comes with dates residents can act on. UDNJ's Mega Diwali 2026 runs Saturday, October 24 from noon to 8:30 p.m., with live performances, dancing, Garba, food, crafts and vendors, concluding with fireworks; Bhasin invited officials, residents and families of all backgrounds. The township's own Diwali lighting ceremony follows on Friday, October 30 at 6:30 p.m. near the gazebo at the East Brunswick Municipal Complex, 1 Civic Center Drive, with refreshments served. Both events are open to the wider community, and Diwali itself — with the Hindu New Year — falls in early November, closing a festival month that began with Navratri, Durga Puja and Dussehra.
